name: Currency Hedging
title: Currency Hedging
answer: Currency hedging covers the practice of using financial instruments to offset the effect of exchange rate movements on a company's cash flows, balance sheet, or forecast transactions. In treasury it sits alongside cash management, liquidity forecasting, and interest rate risk, and it applies wherever a business earns, spends, borrows, or holds money in more than one currency. The work spans policy setting, exposure identification, instrument selection, execution, and ongoing measurement of hedge effectiveness.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Currency hedging covers the practice of using financial instruments to offset the effect of exchange rate movements on a company's cash flows, balance sheet, or forecast transactions. In treasury it sits alongside cash management, liquidity forecasting, and interest rate risk, and it applies wherever a business earns, spends, borrows, or holds money in more than one currency. The work spans policy setting, exposure identification, instrument selection, execution, and ongoing measurement of hedge effectiveness.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The core systems are the treasury management system, the enterprise resource planning ledger, and the market data feeds that supply spot and forward rates. Banks provide execution and confirmation channels, while accounting and reporting modules capture the resulting entries under the relevant accounting standard. Increasingly, exposure data is pulled from multiple ledgers and reconciled automatically rather than assembled by hand in spreadsheets.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Treasury teams start by mapping exposures, separating contractual items such as invoices and debt from forecast items such as expected sales. They then apply the hedge policy, which sets which currencies and exposure types are covered, the permitted instruments, and the target hedge ratios. Forwards are the common instrument, with options and cross currency swaps used where the policy allows. Effectiveness is tested and documented, and the results feed into the monthly close and into reports to management.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Hedging sits under a board approved policy that defines authority, limits, counterparty criteria, and prohibited instruments such as outright speculation. Documentation must support hedge accounting treatment, and audit and internal control functions test that trades match the stated exposure and that valuations are independently checked. Counterparty credit risk, collateral calls, and the possibility of over hedging are monitored continuously, and any breach of limits is escalated through a defined channel.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Automation is shifting routine exposure gathering, trade suggestion, and effectiveness testing from manual work toward systems that reconcile positions and flag policy breaches in near real time. That raises questions about who approves an automated trade and how the audit trail is preserved. Expect more attention to data lineage, to the treatment of forecast exposures, and to how treasury systems explain their own recommendations to controllers and auditors.
